title: A Paired-Phase Construction for Ordinary Binary Polynomial Multiplication
author: Árpád Csizmadia

problem.input: two ascending coefficient-bit lists of length n, representing degree-less-than-n polynomials
problem.output: all 2n-1 ascending product coefficient bits, including zeros
problem.size_parameter: n is the number of coefficient bits in each operand
problem.uniformity: one deterministic machine for every n; constants and cutoff independent of n
problem.model: fixed finite alphabet and fixed finite number of one-dimensional sequential tapes
problem.cost: worst-case machine transitions, including input/output, setup, arithmetic, conversions, tape movement and workspace cleanup

evidence.basis: written all-size proof with technical appendices
evidence.finite_certificates_scope: fixed root geometry, binary fitting, five-stage bank identity, orthogonal rectangle partition and strict rank moment only

artifacts.integrity_command_scope: offline package, source/PDF binding and recorded finite-certificate hash checks; does not verify the all-size theorem

scope.included: ordinary F2 multiplication and explicit fixed-operand transpose
scope.external_inputs: Harvey-van der Hoeven deterministic cyclotomic host/root construction and classical fixed-tape Schonhage-Strassen multiplication for auxiliary products
scope.local_interfaces: finite construction, integer composition, rational movement, native endpoint tensors, local algebra and ordinary reduction in Appendices A-G

ai_assistance.scope: mathematical development, source inspection, finite-certificate code, writing and internal review; internal AI review is not external human verification
